newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to regroup, seen trying $2,440.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to regroup, seen trying $2,440.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices are likely to pause temporarily above the $2,400 level but will eventually challenge $2,440 - the 1997 high, analysts said.
Aluminium is struggling somewhat on the upside despite healthy stock drawdowns and may revert towards $1,650, they added.
Tuesday's strong advances petered out $7 below the talismanic $2,440 level, although the close was technically constructive above $2,408, a recent double-top chart objective.

Traders said that once the market consolidates for an interim period, the uptrend will be resumed. Ammunition for this bullish view was data on Tuesday from the International Copper Study Group, which said Jan/Feb consumption rose 7.5 percent year-on-year.
LME trader Brandeis said that this, as well as the ongoing production setbacks, have served to underline the continued tight supply/demand balance.
"On the charts a series of constructive closes suggests that a serious test of resistance at this year's high of $2,440 is likely with the next barrier at $2,500," Brandeis said.
At 0855 three months prices were indicated at a little changed $2,412/15.
The market's continued difficulty overhead means that a period of consolidation is needed, unless there is a powerful drive in the copper market, traders added.

"$1,680 is proving to be the next level of resistance. However, with the technical ,indicators struggling to extend upwards further consolidation is expected," analyst Martin Squires of LME trader Rudolf Wolff said.
Brandeis said that on the candlestick charts, the market had formed another "doji" (opening and closing at the same level).
"The market has tried to move higher for the last four days and failed. It may come back to test support at $1,635, with the next downside target seen at $1,615," Brandeis added.
At 0855 aluminium was quoted at $1,664/66, down around $5 from Tuesday.
